source_caption:
🎬 42 (2013)

42 tells the inspiring true story of Jackie Robinson, the legendary baseball player who broke Major League Baseball’s modern-era color barrier in 1947. After being recruited by Brooklyn Dodgers executive Branch Rickey, Jackie faces intense racism, discrimination, and hostility from opposing players, fans, and even some teammates. Despite overwhelming pressure, he refuses to let hatred destroy his dream and proves his talent through determination, courage, and extraordinary athletic ability. With support from his wife Rachel and those who believe in him, Jackie changes baseball history forever. Combining powerful performances, emotional storytelling, and unforgettable sports moments, the film explores perseverance, equality, sacrifice, and the courage to challenge injustice.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Sports • Drama • History

⭐ IMDb: 7.5/10

⏱️ Runtime: 2h 8m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Brian Helgeland

🏆 Recognition: Starring Chadwick Boseman as Jackie Robinson and Harrison Ford as Branch Rickey, the film celebrates one of baseball’s most important historical figures. Robinson’s number 42 was retired across Major League Baseball in 1997.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: 42 is a 2013 American biographical film produced by Legendary Pictures and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. Written and directed by Brian Helgeland, 42 is based on baseball player Jackie Robinson, the first black athlete to play in Major League Baseball (MLB) during the modern era. The title of the film reflects Robinson's jersey number, which was universally retired across all MLB teams in 1997. The ensemble cast includes Chadwick Boseman as Robinson, alongside Harrison Ford, Nicole Beharie, Christopher Meloni, André Holland, Lucas Black, Hamish Linklater, and Alan Tudyk in supporting roles.
